newsitem.title: JAPAN: NatWest says negotiating to buy Citicorp TSE seat.
newsitem.headline: NatWest says negotiating to buy Citicorp TSE seat.

text.p: NatWest Securities Japan Ltd said on Friday that it was negotiating with Citicorp International Securities Ltd to buy Citicorp's memberships on the Tokyo Stock Exchange (TSE) and on the Osaka Securities Exchange (OSE).

The securities unit of Britain's National Westminster Bank Plc aims to finalise the deal by the end of November and take over the seats by the end of the year, said Shichiro Hattori, director of Japan for NatWest Markets, a National Westminster Bank group company.
The New York-based Citicorp unit said in August that it would pull out of Japan's equity markets.
NatWest Securities previously held a TSE membership, but sold it in April 1993 and halted securities transactions in Japan except for bond trading.
"We decided to return...to meet demand from investors who hold global portfolios," Hattori said.
NatWest Securities will increase its capital, which has dropped sharply due to cumulative losses, by 10 billion yen to 14.5 billion yen, he said.
Hattori declined to disclose a price for the TSE seat, but Jiji news agency said NatWest was likely to pay about 800 million yen for the seat. No price was given for the OSE seat.
